concurrent_worker_fusion.reason: A newer parallel worker installed an admitted V15 singleton presence implementation before this worker could safely wire its alternative. The stale duplicate files were removed instead of being allowed to fork architecture.

hypothesis: A single monotonic presence lease with privacy-preserving BUSY and fencing is a suitable semantic singleton primitive for Frank v0.1.
strongest_counterhypothesis: TTL expiry can admit a successor while an old process is still physically executing; DB heartbeat/release fencing alone does not prove zero overlap of cognition/tools/effects.

external_evidence.finding: BEGIN IMMEDIATE supplies short atomic write admission while WAL permits concurrent readers; do not hold a full-task write transaction.
exclusive nonblocking flock is a one-host physical exclusion candidate and releases when the holder's file descriptors close/process exits.
time-bounded leases require care for slow/live clients; fencing tokens are recommended and lock ownership cannot be assumed for arbitrary work after expiry.

out_of_box_experiment.name: ghost-holder fencing
out_of_box_experiment.mechanism: allow an old lease to expire, admit a successor with a higher epoch, then attempt stale heartbeat and release from the ghost holder
out_of_box_experiment.interpretation: supports semantic fencing but does not close the separate live-process-overlap counterhypothesis

architecture_delta.candidate: retain current V15 semantic presence lease; falsify live-but-expired overlap; compare per-step epoch revalidation vs Linux flock+semantic fencing on current one-host target
architecture_delta.rollback: current V15 source remains canonical until a stronger measured candidate is promoted
